prompt: A paper-doll parts sheet, in exactly the painting style of Figure 1, of five separate lost household things for a storybook, all painted at one shared scale as if lying side by side, with wide empty space between them, none touching. Their heights relative to the ladder: the kite with its tail is four fifths of the ladder's height, the sock three fifths, and the key and the spool each half. A little wooden ladder with five rungs standing upright, with two sturdy pale-wood rails, three times as tall as it is wide, the tallest thing on the sheet. A diamond-shaped paper kite of faded rust-red and cream patches on a thin wooden cross, with a short tail of three cloth bows joined to its bottom corner, the whole kite with its tail one and a half times as tall as it is wide, no string. A wooden spool wound thick with sage-green thread, standing upright, as tall as it is wide, its loose end tucked in. A single cream wool sock with rust and sage stripes and a darned heel, lying flat, twice as tall as it is wide. An old brass key with a round looped bow, standing upright, two and a half times as tall as it is wide. Leave a wide margin of empty paper on all four sides. Each piece is complete, with a clean hard edge. No cast shadows on the paper. Hand-painted traditional watercolor with a fine graphite pencil outline, from a vintage natural history picture book. Soft pigment washes, visible paper grain, gentle edges. Natural, believable objects, not cartoons. On plain flat solid vivid magenta paper, one even color. No pink or purple on any object. No scenery, no text.

Figure 1 shows a wooden spool wound with sage-green thread, painted on magenta paper. Paint exactly the same spool again, in exactly the same painting style and colors, as a single die-cut paper piece, flat-on and upright: the same pale wooden flanges, the same sage-green thread, and the same loose end of thread curling off to one side. The spool alone, centered, and large: its height is half the height of the image, and it is about as tall as it is wide. Leave a wide margin of empty paper on all four sides, with nothing touching the edge of the image. Its silhouette has a clean hard edge traced with a fine graphite pencil outline. No cast shadows on the paper. Hand-painted traditional watercolor with a fine graphite pencil outline, from a vintage natural history picture book. Soft pigment washes, visible paper grain, gentle edges. On plain flat solid vivid magenta paper, one even color. No pink or purple on the spool. No scenery, no text.
